population.definition: Estimate for the city (not metropolitan area) for 1 July 2018, attributed on citypopulation.de to the UN World Urbanization Prospects 2018 Revision. Eritrea has had no recent census: the last (1984) is cited as 275,385 for the city on the same page. Other sources differ widely; EBSCO cites a CIA World Factbook estimate of 1.073 million for 2023.

facts.claim: Asmara was founded on the site of four ancient villages, collectively called Arbate Asmara.

source.author: Edward Denison
source.date: 2018 (PDF metadata; summarises the Jan 2016 nomination dossier)
source.quote: Asmara was founded on the site where an agglomeration of four ancient villages, ‘Arbate Asmara’, had existed for centuries.

facts.claim: Asmara's name derives from a legend of women from four villages uniting; the dossier glosses it as 'They (the women) united them (the villages)'. Dates for the legend are traditional, not documented (EBSCO places four Tigrinya tribes at Asmara by the 12th century in traditional legend).

facts.claim: Italian forces occupied Asmara in 1889, and Italy moved its colonial capital there from Massawa in 1900. (EBSCO instead says Asmara became the colonial empire's cultural capital in 1897: sources differ.)

places.name: Medeber Market (Medebar)
places.what: An open-air workshop market where metalworkers and other artisans turn scrap and discarded materials into household items. Eritrean Ministry of Information articles describe it as a former caravan trade post; whether it lies inside the UNESCO-inscribed perimeter is not confirmed by a readable source.

source.title: Asmara's Marketplaces: Vibrant Hubs Reflecting Eritrea's Rich Heritage
source.author: Luwam Kahsay H.
source.date: 2025-05-10 (page shows last updated 2026-06-12)
source.quote: Medeber, the self-proclaimed "creative workshop of Eritrea," stands as a powerful testament to ingenuity and sustainability.

places.name: Enda Mariam Orthodox Cathedral (St Mary's)
places.what: The main Eritrean Orthodox cathedral in Asmara, built in 1938 in a modernist idiom that draws on highland building traditions. It stands in the former mixed zone of the Italian-era city, which falls inside the UNESCO-inscribed historic centre (inference from the nomination paper: the paper places the nominated property as the Italian-era centre and describes St Mary's in the mixed zone).

places.name: Eritrean Railway (Asmara to Massawa line)
places.what: A narrow-gauge line built under Italian rule that climbs from the Red Sea coast to the highland capital. It was damaged and abandoned in the 1970s war years and rehabilitated after independence by veteran railway workers; the line as a whole runs outside the inscribed perimeter, station location not verified.

places.name: National Museum of Eritrea
places.what: Eritrea's national museum, inaugurated in 1992 in Asmara's old government palace. It has paleontological, archaeological, art, natural history, medieval history and ethnography sections. Perimeter status not verified.
